lines.say: This fluffy cloud | weighs as much as | a-hundred elephants.
lines.show: This fluffy cloud | weighs as much as | 100 elephants.

lines.say: So how is it | just hanging up there?
A typical puffy cloud | is about a kilometer | wide, tall and deep.
Each cubic meter holds | just half a gram | of water. | Not even a sip.
But this cloud | holds a billion | cubic meters.
Add it all up, | and five-hundred tonnes | of water are floating | over your head.
lines.show: Add it all up, | and 500 tonnes | of water are floating | over your head.

lines.say: So why doesn't it fall? | It does. | Just very slowly.
The water is split | into droplets so tiny | they sink about | a centimeter a second.
And warm air | rising from the ground | pushes up | hundreds of times faster, | so it keeps | carrying them back up.
Besides, the air | in that same space | weighs about | a-thousand times more | than the water.
lines.show: Besides, the air | in that same space | weighs about | 1,000 times more | than the water.

lines.say: Next to it, | the cloud is a lightweight.
Until the droplets | start crashing | into each other.
A million of them | make one raindrop. | Too heavy to float, | it falls.
And the hundred elephants | come down on you, | one drop at a time.
lines.show: And the 100 elephants | come down on you, | one drop at a time.
